sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Security headers on login page
sections.what: Checks the login page response includes the frame blocking, content type and content security settings, and does not reveal the server software.
sections.why: Locks in basic web protections that are easy to lose during changes.
sections.watch_out: Only the login page is tested, so other routes need their own checks if they must be protected too.

summary: A single browser-level test that checks the login page sends the expected security headers.
purpose: Confirms the app tells browsers to block clickjacking, to not guess content types, and to hide its server software.
why: These response headers are a cheap defence against common web attacks, and removing one by accident is easy.
how: It requests the login page directly and reads its response headers. It checks the content security policy allows no framing, the frame option is set to deny, content type sniffing is off, and the powered-by header is absent.
inputs: A request to the login page.
outputs: Pass or fail for each header.
risks: Only the login page is checked, so other pages could drop the headers without the test noticing.
debug: If a header is missing, check the server or middleware configuration that sets headers for all routes.
